culture_format.note: All 24 wells are 2D: each group needs its 6 wells for the four lab assays. 3D (spheroids in low-attachment wells) needs a second cassette, a flight-2 option.

brief.wants: Better biological protection against microgravity- and space-radiation-induced cellular damage.
brief.problem: The space environment induces oxidative stress, inflammation, cellular senescence and functional deterioration.
brief.evidence: Spaceflight research has documented cellular and molecular alterations associated with microgravity and radiation exposure.
brief.why: These effects can compromise astronaut health, particularly during long-duration missions.
brief.in_scope: WJ-MSCs vs Muse cells, with and without exosomes, under spaceflight conditions, with radiation dosimetry and live-cell monitoring.
brief.out_of_scope: Human treatment or clinical administration during this experiment.

roles.does: automated culture, fluidics and flight hardware
roles.here: module 17, built to the LELP-1 bay interface
Space Philic: RUPAK launch, LELP-1 operations, dosimetry, whole-lab return

brief.expected: Whether Muse cells are more resilient than WJ-MSCs, and whether exosomes reduce space-induced cellular damage.

blockers.answer: Module 17 is designed to the LELP-1 large-bay interface: 6.0 kg, 22 W peak, 24 wells, BSL-2 triple containment, checked against the lab's limits.
37 °C thaw block, 3 pumps and 5 reservoirs on a timer; Sentinel refuses a thaw into a cold block.
One large bay on LELP-1 for 7 days, launched by RUPAK; the whole lab comes home.
Ground tests the twin points to: thaw and DMSO wash without a centrifuge, GSH/NAD stability at 4 °C, imaging dose, per-well segmentation.
